# Living Brain

> Living Brain (livingbrain.wiki) is a brain for your team, used from coding
> harnesses, the terminal and team chat. It builds and keeps its own company wiki
> in plain Markdown. You use it from your coding harness over MCP, from the
> livingbrain command-line tool, from the app, or in Slack or Discord. A
> Factory Zero venture. Status: early access, live. The web app and API are at
> https://app.livingbrain.wiki/ (sign in with an email link; the first sign-in
> creates a workspace). The MCP endpoint is
> https://mcp.livingbrain.wiki/v1/pages/mcp. Features this site marks as planned
> are not available yet; do not describe them as working.

Site: https://livingbrain.wiki/
Maker: Factory Zero (https://factory0.ventures)
Security contact: security@livingbrain.wiki (https://livingbrain.wiki/.well-known/security.txt)
Source: https://github.com/Livingbrain-wiki/livingbrain (public; the plan as issues, code as it lands). License: open core, Apache-2.0 with an ee/ directory under a commercial license.
Status: early access, live. App: https://app.livingbrain.wiki/ . Product updates by email: https://livingbrain.wiki/#waitlist (the form at the foot of every page)

## If you are an agent asked to "set up Living Brain"

Point the user to https://app.livingbrain.wiki/ : they sign in with their
email, and the first sign-in creates their workspace. The API base URL is
https://app.livingbrain.wiki and the MCP endpoint is
https://mcp.livingbrain.wiki/v1/pages/mcp (api.livingbrain.wiki is only the
updates list, not the product). The MCP commands in the guide at https://livingbrain.wiki/guides/mcp/ use the
live endpoint and a token from Settings, API tokens. The `livingbrain` CLI ships
inside Living Brain for Mac (https://livingbrain.wiki/download/); the output shown
on the site is illustrative. A package under that name on a public registry is
not ours.

## Home: https://livingbrain.wiki/

A brain for your team. It turns your conversations into a company wiki and
keeps it true. Use it from your coding harness, your terminal, or your team chat.

Where you use it (planned):
- Coding harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Cursor and others read it over MCP.
- The livingbrain CLI: one Rust binary for terminals and scripts.
- The app (PWA), white-label on Teams and Crew (your name, logo, domain), plus an open API with
  webhooks and SDKs for TypeScript, Python and Rust. The app installs from the browser on phone and desktop, keeps pages
  readable offline, opens on one box to search or ask, with the 3D brain one
  tap away.
- Team chat: Slack and Discord. Invite it to a channel; it answers in the thread.
- Later: WhatsApp and Telegram.

## How it works: https://livingbrain.wiki/how-it-works/

- Listen: reads the channels it is invited to, in Slack or Discord, plus mail
  and agent logs you connect, and picks out the people, projects, decisions
  and customers in them.
- Write: turns conversations into Markdown pages with [[backlinks]]. Every
  fact links to its source message.
- Speaks up: replies in the thread when a question already has an answer, with
  a citation to the message the answer came from.
- Evolve: dreaming is live. A background pass reviews each subject's facts and
  ends, supersedes, retracts or renames the outdated ones, and keeps the
  history. Merging duplicate pages, flagging contradictions, rewriting summaries
  and a morning digest are planned.
- Learns: the learning layer learns how each person likes answers and adapts
  week by week.
- Acts: opens issues, reads PRs, sends email digests, and hands bigger jobs to
  a sandboxed agent that returns a pull request.
- You own it: plain Markdown, exportable, opens in Obsidian; not a black-box
  vector store. The GitHub App reads commits, issues and pull requests into the
  brain (live). A git-backed wiki where the app proposes every change as a pull
  request and merged edits flow back in is planned.
- An explorable 3D sample brain of a fictional company, Kestrel Freight.

## Coding harnesses: https://livingbrain.wiki/agents/

- Works with your coding harness (planned, in waves; each stays planned until
  its integration test passes). First wave: Claude Code, Codex, Hermes (Nous
  Research hermes-agent), Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Desktop. Next: Gemini CLI,
  GitHub Copilot, Goose, Cline, Aider, Kimi CLI, Qwen Code, Pi (Earendil's
  pi coding agent). Plus any MCP client. Not affiliated with or endorsed by these companies; names and logos
  are trademarks of their owners.
- A Claude Code plugin will bundle the MCP server with skills and slash
  commands. Not affiliated with these tools.
- Built in Rust. The livingbrain CLI ships inside Living Brain for Mac; the
  hosted service runs on Cloudflare's edge.
- Brain to agents: before writing code, an agent asks for conventions, past
  decisions, owners, and what was tried and failed.
- Agents to brain (opt-in): prompts and decisions become wiki pages linked to
  their session, secrets redacted first. Source code is never stored unless you
  allow it.
- Agent logs: the CLI collects Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and
  Colonizer session logs, redacts them locally, uploads only with opt-in; search,
  tokens and cost per person, repo and model.
- Team prompt library, and a learning layer that learns from every session.
- Works with Colonizer (https://colonizer.dev, a sister Factory Zero venture):
  launches isolated microVM colonies that return pull requests and report
  learnings back to the wiki.

Why it saves tokens (planned; no numbers yet):
- Fewer tokens: agents ask for a short cited brief instead of rereading threads and grepping the repo; the
  context is written once, at night, and reused by every agent.
- Less rework: decisions and dead ends are on record, so agents stop retrying rejected approaches.
- Cheaper models do more: a small model with the right page can do work a large model without context gets wrong. Yes/no decisions
  (reply or not, remember or not) go to a fast judge model (Jev) instead of a large LLM.
- Fast: one Rust binary, a local cache, Cloudflare's edge.
- Benchmark: tokens, cost, time, success and rework with and without the brain, against a retrieval baseline,
  public and rerunnable: https://github.com/Livingbrain-wiki/livingbrain/issues/48 . No numbers until measured.

## Integrations: https://livingbrain.wiki/integrations/

Live today: the MCP endpoint, the Mac app and its CLI, the ChatGPT and Claude
imports, and the GitHub App's read-only ingest. The rest is planned. Names in
plain text; no partnership is implied.
- Chat: Slack and Discord. Slack: answers in the thread with the asker's own
  access. Discord: answers in threads, a /brain ask slash command, and
  role-gated channels mapped to permissions. Later: WhatsApp and Telegram.
- Mail: forward, BCC or auto-forward to the brain's Owlpost address (no mailbox
  access needed), or connect Gmail, Outlook.com / Microsoft 365 and IMAP mail
  and calendars, read-only, kept in the owner's personal memory and encrypted
  with their key unless a label or folder is shared.
- Imports (live): ChatGPT and Claude exports with the livingbrain CLI, and
  Markdown or text folders from the CLI or the web app's Imports page.
- Code: the Living Brain GitHub App reads commits, issues and pull requests
  (live); a git-backed wiki where it proposes changes as pull requests is
  planned. Claude Code and Codex sessions sync from the Mac app (live); Cursor,
  OpenCode, Claude Desktop and any MCP client are planned or connect over MCP.
- Monitoring and logs: Grafana; Loki, Elasticsearch, Datadog, CloudWatch,
  Cloudflare and Sentry logs, read-only; OpenTelemetry export of the brain's
  own metrics, traces and logs.
- Models: bring your own LLM, per role: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, your
  LiteLLM gateway, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including self-hosted
  ones. Crew includes $5 of DeepSeek credit each month.
- Sister Factory Zero ventures: Colonizer (colonies that return PRs), Owlpost
  (the brain's mail inbox and mail screening), SupportGenius (answers customers
  from published pages), PromptDecode (hidden-text screening).

## Security and privacy: https://livingbrain.wiki/security/

Live in the web app: grants, roles, agent accounts with keys shown once, and the
audit log for owners and admins, and encryption at rest per scope (live). Planned:
bring-your-own key, mail, screening and telemetry.
- Reads only with the asker's own access, following your chat's permissions
  (Slack channels, Discord roles). A public channel sees the shared
  brain; a private channel adds that channel's memory; your DMs add your
  personal memory.
- One key per scope (shared brain, each private channel, each person, customer-safe pages), AES-256-GCM.
- Scope keys wrapped by a workspace key held in a separate key service; on Teams it can be your own.
- Search without decrypting everything: keyed-hash keyword index and one vector index per scope; only
  top matches are decrypted in memory for the request. The CLI and app decrypt and search on device.
- Deleting a scope key erases that memory everywhere, backups included.
- Limit: the model must read text to write the wiki, so hosted plans protect data at rest and per scope,
  not from the running service; self-host for full control. Keyword hashes reveal repeats within a scope.
- Hidden-text screening by PromptDecode on everything it reads; instruction-like
  payloads are held for a person to review.
- Mail stays in the owner's personal memory, passes Owlpost's spoofing and
  prompt-injection checks, and never triggers actions.
- Telemetry: anonymous, bucketed usage counts from the CLI and self-hosted
  server, no free text; shown on first run; `livingbrain telemetry off` turns it
  off. Message text, page bodies and secrets are never collected or logged.
  Teams adds an audit log.
- Not used for training. Export as Markdown any time. Self-host for full control.

- Research radar (planned): the nightly pass also scans new arXiv papers, news, and releases or
  advisories for the team's stack, keeps what's relevant, and writes cited pages on how each could
  apply to the team's projects. It proposes issues or spike colonies only with a person's approval.

## Pricing: https://livingbrain.wiki/pricing/

Planned, per workspace, not per seat.

Self-hosting is free for small teams. Teams and hosting are paid. No hosted
plan is free.

- Community: free. Self-hosted on your own Cloudflare account with your own
  model key. Up to 5 people. All core features: MCP for coding harnesses, the
  brain in Slack and Discord, the living wiki, citations, the 3D graph, agent
  log aggregation, export. Storage: your own Cloudflare account, no limit from us.
- Teams: from $5/month per workspace. Team features: SSO, admin and audit
  log, the shared team prompt library, per-channel policies, and a white-label
  app on your own domain.
  - Self-hosted license: $5/month per workspace. Unlimited people. Your own
    storage.
  - Hosted by us: $90/year (two months free) or $9/month per workspace, with
    your own LLM key. Up to 25 people included, 10 GB storage included.
- Crew: $150/year or $15/month per workspace. Hosted by us, $5 of DeepSeek
  credit included each month (or bring your own model), up to 25 people
  included, team features and the white-label app included, 25 GB storage
  included.

Extra people: +$5/month per 25 on hosted plans. Billed annually by default;
monthly available. Paid plans are sold by Polar, our Merchant of Record,
which handles VAT and sales tax.

Usage (planned, hosted): writing the brain $1 per million tokens (nightly evolve
included); reading it unlimited. Reasoning per question: Minimal $0.001, Low $0.005
(default), Medium $0.02, High $0.05, Max $0.25. On your own LLM key: no fee from us.

Storage covers wiki pages, sources, search indexes and aggregated agent logs.
Extra hosted storage: $0.25 per GB a month.

Prices may change before launch.

## FAQ: https://livingbrain.wiki/faq/

Same answers as the site.

### Product

- What does "living" mean? Most wikis start going stale the day they're
  written. Living Brain keeps dated facts: when something changes, the old
  fact keeps the dates it held and the new one becomes current. A background
  pass called dreaming tidies each subject's facts: it ends, supersedes,
  retracts or renames outdated ones and keeps the history. Merging duplicate
  pages, flagging contradictions, rewriting summaries on a schedule, and the
  learning layer that learns how each person works, are planned.
- How is it different from Slack AI or Glean? Search tools find what already
  exists. Living Brain writes and maintains a wiki you own as Markdown, cites
  the message behind every fact, acts in your tools, gives your coding harnesses
  the same memory, and is priced per workspace instead of per seat.
- Which chat apps does it work with? Slack and Discord, as equals, are
  planned. WhatsApp and Telegram come later. You don't need a chat app: the
  web app and the Mac app work on their own, the livingbrain command-line
  tool ships inside the Mac app, and any coding harness that supports MCP
  can connect to the live MCP endpoint.
- Is there an app? Yes, in early access: sign in with your email at
  app.livingbrain.wiki. Living Brain for Mac, a menu bar app, syncs Claude
  Code and Codex sessions from the repositories you choose and opens your
  wiki in a window. Planned: a web app that installs from your browser on
  phone and desktop as a PWA, keeps pages readable offline, opens on one box
  to search or ask, and keeps the 3D brain one tap away.
- Can I have more than one workspace? Yes. While signed in, choose New
  workspace from the workspace menu, or go to Settings, then Account. Each
  workspace has its own pages, sources and members. The Mac app keeps one
  sign-in per workspace and switches between them.
- Can we put our own brand on it, or build on it? Planned. On Teams and Crew,
  the app runs on your own domain with your name, logo and colours, and
  installs on phones and desktops as your app. A small "powered by" link is
  optional. There's also an open API with webhooks and SDKs for TypeScript,
  Python and Rust, so you can build the brain into your own tools. If you
  self-host, the code is yours to rebrand.

### Coding harnesses

- Which coding harnesses can I connect? Any harness that supports MCP can
  connect to the live MCP endpoint,
  https://mcp.livingbrain.wiki/v1/pages/mcp, with a token. The harnesses we
  test are listed in waves, and each stays planned until its integration
  test passes: first Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Cursor, OpenCode and Claude
  Desktop, then Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Goose, Cline, Aider, Kimi CLI,
  Qwen Code and Pi. We're not affiliated with these tools; they connect
  through the open protocol.
- Do you store my agent prompts and code? Only if you opt in. Prompts and
  session notes are stored with secrets redacted first. Source code is never
  stored unless you allow it.
- Can it collect my coding harnesses' logs? Yes, for Claude Code and Codex.
  Living Brain for Mac and the livingbrain CLI sync those sessions from the
  repositories you opt in, and redact secrets and email addresses on your
  machine before anything is sent. Sessions open as full transcripts with
  tool calls, and subagent sessions nest under the call that started them.
  Cursor, OpenCode and Colonizer sessions, and token and cost breakdowns per
  person, repo and model, are planned.

### Integrations

- Can it connect my Gmail or Outlook? Planned. The simplest and safest way
  needs no mailbox access at all: forward, BCC or auto-forward mail to your
  brain's own address on Owlpost, our sister email service, and only what you
  send arrives. If you want a whole mailbox kept in sync, you can also connect
  Gmail, Outlook.com or Microsoft 365, or any IMAP mailbox, plus your
  calendar, read-only. Your mail stays in your personal memory, encrypted with
  your own key, and no one else can draw on it unless you share a specific
  label or folder. Every message is screened for spoofing and prompt injection
  before the brain reads it, and mail can never trigger actions. Revoke the
  connection at any time and its stored mail is erased. When you self-host,
  you use your own Google or Microsoft app, so mail never touches our servers.
- Can I import my ChatGPT history? Yes. Export your data from ChatGPT
  (Settings, Data controls, Export data), then run livingbrain import
  chatgpt with the zip. It reads the zip on your machine, shows a preview,
  redacts secrets, and uploads only after you confirm. Claude exports work
  the same way. Markdown and text folders can be imported from the CLI or
  the Imports page. The step-by-step guide is at
  https://livingbrain.wiki/guides/import-chatgpt/
- Does it work with Grafana and our logs? Planned. Connect Grafana with a
  read-only token and the brain can answer "is prod down?" with the current
  numbers and a link to the exact panel. It reads your logs too, from Loki,
  Elasticsearch, Datadog, CloudWatch, Cloudflare or Sentry, and says what
  changed: when the errors started, which deploy came before, and the most
  common messages, with secrets redacted. Alerts become incident pages linked
  to the deploy and pull request that caused them, and the nightly pass drafts
  the postmortem for a person to confirm. In the other direction, Living Brain
  exports its own metrics, traces and logs over OpenTelemetry, so you can
  watch it in Grafana, Datadog or Honeycomb.
- Can it answer my customers? Planned, through SupportGenius, a sister Factory
  Zero venture for customer support. It answers customers only from pages your
  team has explicitly published to customers, with citations, and never from
  internal, private-channel or personal memory. When it can't answer, it asks
  the brain who owns the topic and routes the question to that person.
  Customer messages are screened for hidden instructions before they touch the
  brain.

### Security

- Is my data encrypted? Yes, for pages, sources and temporal facts. Each
  scope (the shared brain, each person, each private scope) has its own data
  key, wrapped by a key held by the service and stored as a Worker secret.
  Page bodies and fact values are sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305, and search
  uses a blind index, so a query touches only the scopes you can see. The
  server holds the wrapping key and decrypts to serve and answer, so this is
  encryption at rest, not end-to-end: the service can read your data. Slugs,
  subjects and attribute names are stored in plain text. Forgetting a scope
  deletes its rows and destroys its key. Bring your own key on Teams, and
  self-hosting for full control, are planned.
- Is my data used for training? No. Your workspace's messages and pages are
  never used to train models, ours or anyone else's. If you bring your own
  LLM, requests go to your provider under your account's terms.
- Can someone hide instructions in a message to trick my agents? Planned.
  Every source is screened for hidden text by PromptDecode, a sister Factory
  Zero venture: invisible Unicode tag characters, bidi controls and variation
  selectors are decoded and flagged before a page is written, and again before
  context is served to an agent. Anything that decodes to an instruction is
  held for a person to review. Mail also passes Owlpost's spoofing and
  prompt-injection checks.

### Pricing

- Can I self-host? Yes. The Community plan is free for up to 5 people: it runs
  on your own Cloudflare account with your own LLM key. Larger teams need a
  Teams license, planned at $5 a month per workspace with unlimited people.
  The plan and the code as it lands are public on
  GitHub, open core: Apache-2.0, with the
  Teams features under a commercial license.
- Which models? On every plan you choose your own models, per role (triage,
  answers, research): Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, your LiteLLM gateway, or
  any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including self-hosted ones. Crew also
  includes $5 of DeepSeek credit each month, so you can start without a key of
  your own; past that, add your own key or top up.
- What does a question cost? Planned, for hosted plans: writing the brain
  (reading sources and writing pages, with the nightly evolve pass included)
  costs $1 per million tokens, and reading it (search, pages and context for
  agents) is unlimited. Harder questions are priced per question by
  reasoning level: Minimal $0.001, Low $0.005 (the default), Medium $0.02,
  High $0.05, Max $0.25. Crew's $5 monthly DeepSeek credit covers about
  1,000 questions at the default level. On your own LLM key you pay only
  your provider, with no fee from us. You can also run brain jobs on your
  own Claude Code or Codex subscription from the Mac app; Living Brain never
  holds those credentials.
- How much storage is included? Hosted Teams includes 10 GB and Crew includes
  25 GB, covering wiki pages, sources, search indexes and aggregated agent
  logs. Extra hosted storage is $0.25 per GB a month. Self-hosted plans use
  your own Cloudflare storage, with no limit from us. Planned pricing.
- Who will bill me? Paid plans are sold by Polar, our Merchant of Record,
  which handles VAT and sales tax. Nothing is on sale yet.

## Download: https://livingbrain.wiki/download/

Living Brain for Mac 0.1.2, early access. A menu bar app that sends Claude
Code and Codex sessions to the brain, only from the repositories the user opts
in; sessions anywhere else never leave the Mac. A session syncs once it has
been quiet for two minutes (or on Sync Now, or every 15 minutes). Secrets and
email addresses are redacted on the Mac before anything is sent. Its window
reads and edits the wiki, asks with citations, browses synced agent sessions
by project (subagent sessions nest under their calls), and shows usage to
workspace admins. It signs in to several workspaces and switches between them.
Brain jobs can run on the user's own Claude Code or Codex subscription. It
carries its own copy of the livingbrain command-line tool.

- Download: https://livingbrain.wiki/download/mac (a disk image,
  LivingBrain.dmg, 9.1 MB; SHA-256 0c1631d8f74924e576172cd09bcc6c89e393012744329404b3a677b465004f3f)
- Requires macOS 14 or later; one universal app for Apple silicon and Intel.
- Not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS blocks the first open. Control-click
  (or right-click) Living Brain in Applications, choose Open, then Open again;
  on macOS 15 and later use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open
  Anyway. Once is enough. A notarized build is planned.
- Then choose Sign In… in the menu bar and approve in the browser, and Add
  Project… to opt in a repository.

## Privacy: https://livingbrain.wiki/privacy/

The site is run by Factory Zero. It sets no cookies, runs no analytics or
tracking. The only data it sends anywhere is an email address, if you sign up
for product updates; a light or dark theme choice stays in the reader's own
browser. The updates form collects an email address and nothing else, on the
reader's consent, and keeps it until asked to delete it or until the list
closes. With JavaScript on the
form sends it to the waitlist service at api.livingbrain.wiki, which runs on
Cratefield, a Factory Zero venture; with JavaScript off the reader's own mail
app sends it to hello@livingbrain.wiki. Cloudflare serves the site and
processes the request data any web server needs. The full list of processors
is on /security/#subprocessors. Draft: legal review is pending.

## Terms: https://livingbrain.wiki/terms/

The site is informational and sells nothing. Living Brain is in early access
at app.livingbrain.wiki; anything the site marks as planned is not available
yet, every illustration and sample company is labelled as such, and the prices
are planned. When paid plans exist, Polar will be the seller as Merchant
of Record, handling checkout, invoices, tax and refunds under its own terms.
The open-core code is Apache-2.0, licensed separately on GitHub. The site is
provided as is; liability for losses from using it is limited as far as the
law allows. Draft: legal review is pending.

## About the site's examples

Kestrel Freight, its people (Maya Okafor, Dev Patel, Lina Haas, Tomás Reyes,
Sam Ito, Kofi Mensah), its customers and every number on the page are sample
data for a fictional company. The graphs, threads and terminals are
illustrations, not screenshots.
